Crafting can be annoying to figure out so I've been training my character so I can just do it for you guys when you need it. I'll be able to field all kinds of crafting requests soon

but in case you wanna try to do it yourself I'll try to lay out the basics as best I can (a lot of this is guesswork so please forgive me)

ok so to start off crafting is one of the functions of the My room system which is pretty useless to anyone who doesn't have premium because they only give you a tiny room (don't worry about and/or buy premium for this my room is huge and awesome I have lots of games and instruments and stuff and you guys are welcome there anytime so don't waste money on the vanity stuff if you don't really want to) but even on free to play you're still able to craft

you can advertise 3 things you are able to craft and take requests but I'm not really sure what you get in return but not a lot of people bother with crafting so it's a good way to help out your friends and to get the best results for any craft you need to try it a bunch of times to roll a Great Success so there's definitely value in being able to do it for yourself

now there's three things you can do with crafting;

  • Extend Equipment

-ok so this is straight forward at first but then a little complicated basically what this does is upgrade the stats of your equipment you can extend weapons up to 11 star rarity and units can be extended to focus on a certain defense type (there are three types of damage; Stiking, Ranged, and Technique and there's a stat for each one) generally it's just to make lower rarity items usable later in the game but for 10 and 11 star equipment it's a bit different it changes a hidden value on the weapon for your damage variance so instead of doing 90%-100% of the weapons max it switches to 55%-100% this value lessens as you extend more and can even put your damage over 100% but unless your build has a lot of DEX I wouldn't recommend messing with it on better weapons

  • Technique Customization

-ok so this doesn't work on the Photon Arts for the non tech weapons this is only for the spells so unless you're a force, techer, or bouncer it's probably not worth your time but each technique has two available customizations with three possible levels each these are hugely varied from power to range to energy consumption etc. so I'd look into it yourselves if you're really interested but even if you don't want to craft it yourselves these customizations are really valuable and useful so I'd use the visiphone to find someone to customize your favorite techs for you

  • Time Ability Creation

-ok these are super convoluted I'm not even sure I get it myself but I'll try my best basically you can save three possible effects (one for each unit location) that you can create and apply to a unit the effects you get from these are random and complicated and only activate at certain times in certain areas and the effect only stays on the unit for a certain amount of time total the continues counting down even when you're not online.

So generally this is just high level end game over complex shenanigans but if you're really active on the game and spend a lot of time fighting in one specific area and need some specific boost it can be very and weirdly helpful

alright now as for how you learn techniques it's a little complex you learn by doing but certain things you can only pick up from the daily craft requests it gives you and most things require specific practice so once you get around lvl 5-10 crafting wily nily won't get you anywhere anymore so you need to go into the Crafting Achievements section of the crafting menu and look up what and how much of what you need to do to get the recipes you wanna unlock

for the crafting materials there's three ways to get them;

  • Find them while playing

-this is both the easiest and the most annoying while you fight and explore in the field you'll happen upon a lot of materials but it's really annoying to get specific things from this because the drop chances can be irksome

  • Item desynthesis

-this is easy but costly and you don't get a lot of bang for your buck but in the crafting menus there's an option to take apart higher level equipment and techniques for parts this destroys those items so be careful

  • Player shop

-this is costly but fast and reliable you need something? then someone is almost definitely selling it usually pretty cheap but it doesn't matter because you need it in bulk

  • a few extra things

I'd also like to note that for one thing there are room goods you can get to incrementally increase your great success rate or lessen the cool down time from certain crafts but you are only allowed one machine for each kind of crafting

also there are support items you can get to improve 1 specific crafting attempt you can get them from title rewards and scratch tickets

as a last thing you only get a maximum of 3 crafting slots as a free player and you need to level up your crafting to unlock two of them then the next row of slots is only available when you have premium and the third row you can pay real money to unlock and if you are able and willing to spend real money on the game this is one of the few worthwhile things to spend it one (the character inventory size increase is great as well) as it's one of the few things that isn't extraneous or temporary

It's not minimum wage that's broken, but the money itself, and our over-inflation.
